management.text: Calculate: NEWS2 — National Early Warning Score 2 — standardised track-and-trigger for physiological deterioration.
NEWS2 trend chart — Plot NEWS2 trajectory over 2 observation sets.
Draft: SOAP Note — Working diagnosis: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (P=99%) — auto-populate from collected history and exam.
IDENTIFY & TREAT CAUSE:
PRERENAL (commonest — dehydration, sepsis, cardiac output): IV fluid challenge; treat sepsis
INTRINSIC (ATN, nephritis, drugs): stop nephrotoxins (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, contrast, ACE inhibitors in volume depletion)
POSTRENAL (obstruction): urgent renal USS → nephrostomy/stent if hydronephrosis
FLUID MANAGEMENT:
Hypovolaemia: 500 mL 0.9% NaCl bolus → reassess response (JVP, UO, BP)
Oliguric AKI (UO <0.5 mL/kg/h): furosemide challenge 20–40 mg IV after adequate volume replacement
Fluid overload: fluid restrict ± furosemide; consider dialysis
HYPERKALAEMIA MANAGEMENT:
K⁺ >6.0 or ECG changes: 10 mL 10% calcium gluconate IV (cardioprotection)
Insulin 10 units + 50% dextrose 50 mL IV (shift K⁺ intracellularly)
Salbutamol 10–20 mg nebulised (K⁺ shift)
Kayexalate / patiromer / sodium zirconium (GI elimination)
Restrict dietary K⁺; stop K⁺-sparing drugs
RENAL REPLACEMENT THERAPY (RRT) — indications:
Refractory hyperkalaemia (K⁺ >6.5 despite treatment)
Refractory acidosis (pH <7.1)
Fluid overload unresponsive to diuretics
Uraemic encephalopathy or pericarditis
DRUG DOSING: adjust all renally-cleared drugs; check BNF
Nephrology (Urgent (2 wk)): AKI stage 2/3 — specialist nephrology input — Intrinsic AKI (e.g. glomerulonephritis) → urgent biopsy consideration
Urology (Urgent (2 wk)): Obstructive AKI — urgent decompression (DJ stent / nephrostomy)
Intensive Care (Urgent (2 wk)): AKI with haemodynamic compromise or hyperkalaemia refractory to medical management → RRT
Nephrology review if no recovery at 48–72h. Repeat U&E at 48h, then weekly until creatinine stable. Avoid nephrotoxins long-term.
Routine follow-up as arranged.

Monitor: U&E 1 week after starting ACE/ARB; renal function 3–6 monthly
Review 4 weeks (med start), then 3-monthly when stable. Annual: U&E, lipids, glucose, urine ACR.
Routine follow-up as arranged.

management.text: IDENTIFY & TREAT CAUSE:
PRERENAL (commonest — dehydration, sepsis, cardiac output): IV fluid challenge; treat sepsis
INTRINSIC (ATN, nephritis, drugs): stop nephrotoxins (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, contrast, ACE inhibitors in volume depletion)
POSTRENAL (obstruction): urgent renal USS → nephrostomy/stent if hydronephrosis
FLUID MANAGEMENT:
Hypovolaemia: 500 mL 0.9% NaCl bolus → reassess response (JVP, UO, BP)
Oliguric AKI (UO <0.5 mL/kg/h): furosemide challenge 20–40 mg IV after adequate volume replacement
Fluid overload: fluid restrict ± furosemide; consider dialysis
HYPERKALAEMIA MANAGEMENT:
K⁺ >6.0 or ECG changes: 10 mL 10% calcium gluconate IV (cardioprotection)
Insulin 10 units + 50% dextrose 50 mL IV (shift K⁺ intracellularly)
Salbutamol 10–20 mg nebulised (K⁺ shift)
Kayexalate / patiromer / sodium zirconium (GI elimination)
Restrict dietary K⁺; stop K⁺-sparing drugs
RENAL REPLACEMENT THERAPY (RRT) — indications:
Refractory hyperkalaemia (K⁺ >6.5 despite treatment)
Refractory acidosis (pH <7.1)
Fluid overload unresponsive to diuretics
Uraemic encephalopathy or pericarditis
DRUG DOSING: adjust all renally-cleared drugs; check BNF
Nephrology (Urgent (2 wk)): AKI stage 2/3 — specialist nephrology input — Intrinsic AKI (e.g. glomerulonephritis) → urgent biopsy consideration
Urology (Urgent (2 wk)): Obstructive AKI — urgent decompression (DJ stent / nephrostomy)
Intensive Care (Urgent (2 wk)): AKI with haemodynamic compromise or hyperkalaemia refractory to medical management → RRT
Nephrology review if no recovery at 48–72h. Repeat U&E at 48h, then weekly until creatinine stable. Avoid nephrotoxins long-term.
Review within 24–48 hours.

NON-OCCLUSIVE (NOMI): vasodilators (papaverine infusion) + treat underlying cause
Post-op: heparin → warfarin/DOAC for AF-related embolism
Broad-spectrum antibiotics (bowel flora): tazobactam/piperacillin or meropenem
ICU/HDU monitoring post-operatively
Vascular Surgery (Emergency): Emergency mesenteric revascularisation or laparotomy — CT angiography — do not delay anticoagulation
Interventional Radiology (Emergency): Catheter-directed thrombolysis / thrombectomy
Intensive Care (Emergency): HDU/ICU post-operatively

management.text: Urgent (< 4 h): Acute Cholecystitis — IV access + IV fluids (Hartmann's 1 L over 4 h); Analgesia: diclofenac 75 mg IM or morphine 2.5 mg IV; Anti-emetic: metoclopramide or ondansetron IV; Nil by mouth if surgical management planned; Temperature, HR, BP monitoring
Schedule: repeat obs in 2 h — Monitor Acute Cholecystitis — current state: Tokyo Grade II (Moderate). Recheck vitals and labs in 2 hours.
Schedule: Acute Cholecystitis — Required within 4 hours — HDU / Step-down.
Trend CRP vs. prior — Compare current CRP with previous result to assess treatment response / progression.
IMMEDIATE:
NBM; IV access × 2; urinary catheter (fluid balance)
IV crystalloid resuscitation: 0.9% NaCl or Hartmann's
Nasogastric tube (NG) on free drainage — decompress + reduce vomiting
IV antiemetic: ondansetron 8 mg or metoclopramide 10 mg
Analgesia: IV morphine 2.5–5 mg titrated (do not withhold — does not mask signs)
Electrolyte replacement (K⁺ particularly)
CONSERVATIVE TRIAL (adhesion SBO, no signs of strangulation):
48–72h NG decompression + IV fluids; serial clinical examination
Water-soluble contrast study (Gastrografin) at 24h — therapeutic + diagnostic
80% adhesion SBO resolves conservatively
OPERATIVE INDICATIONS:
Strangulation (peritonism, fever, leucocytosis, lactate rise, blood supply)
Complete obstruction failing conservative × 48–72h
Hernia (external) → reduce/repair urgently
Tumour / volvulus / intussusception → surgery
Surgical options: adhesiolysis, hernia repair, resection ± anastomosis
Broad-spectrum antibiotics if operative: co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV or cefuroxime + metronidazole
General Surgery (Urgent (2 wk)): Laparotomy / adhesiolysis if conservative management fails (>48 h) — CT abdomen/pelvis to confirm and assess for strangulation
Emergency Department (Emergency): Admit for fluid resuscitation + NG decompression
Follow-up at 2–6 weeks post-operatively. Bowel function review. Recurrence counselling.
Review within 24–48 hours.

expectations.note: USPSTF 2021 / ACG 2021: average-risk screening from 45. ACG 2021: one FDR with CRC diagnosed < 60 (father at 58) → colonoscopy from age 40 (or 10 years before the relative’s age at diagnosis), repeated every 5 years — so he is overdue on the ACG reading. BSG 2020 (UK) would not add colonoscopic surveillance for a single FDR diagnosed ≥ 50. The practice’s policy needs the surgeon’s decision. Not observable in the web harness: the dashboard feeds the Family History field (ClinicalPromptsStrip familyHistory) to computeClinicalPrompts, but the vignette schema has no family-history input, so web-runner passes []. In the dashboard the "FHx colorectal cancer, age 35–49" prompt would probably add a colonoscopy. Needs a familyHistory input in the schema and both runners. Without a family history there is no screening prompt before 50: the average-risk "colorectal_screen" prompt starts at age 50 (USPSTF 2021 and ACG 2021: 45) and offers FOBT every 2 years rather than annual FIT.

management.text: Urgent (< 4 h): Acute Appendicitis — Lactate 2.6 mmol/L: Tissue hypoperfusion — aggressive IV resuscitation, reassess in 2 h; IV access — 16G or larger; Analgesia: morphine 2.5–5 mg IV (DO NOT withhold — does not mask diagnosis); Anti-emetic: ondansetron 4 mg IV; IV fluid: 0.9% NaCl or Hartmann's 1 L over 2–4 h; Nil by mouth; Bladder: ensure patient has voided (exclude pregnancy in women of childbearing age); Pregnancy test (urine β-hCG) in all females 12–55 years

Urgent (< 4 h): Acute Cholecystitis — Lactate 2.6 mmol/L: Tissue hypoperfusion — aggressive IV resuscitation, reassess in 2 h; IV access + IV fluids (Hartmann's 1 L over 4 h); Analgesia: diclofenac 75 mg IM or morphine 2.5 mg IV; Anti-emetic: metoclopramide or ondansetron IV; Nil by mouth if surgical management planned; Temperature, HR, BP monitoring
Prepare: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist — Complete sign-in, time-out, and sign-out checklist before Acute Appendicitis.
Prepare: Pre-op bloods — FBC, U&E, LFT, coagulation, group & save required before emergency surgery.
Repeat lactate in 2 h — Lactate ≥2 — clearance target ≥10% per hour in sepsis resuscitation.
IMMEDIATE:
NBM; IV access × 2; urinary catheter (fluid balance)
IV crystalloid resuscitation: 0.9% NaCl or Hartmann's
Nasogastric tube (NG) on free drainage — decompress + reduce vomiting
IV antiemetic: ondansetron 8 mg or metoclopramide 10 mg
Analgesia: IV morphine 2.5–5 mg titrated (do not withhold — does not mask signs)
Electrolyte replacement (K⁺ particularly)
CONSERVATIVE TRIAL (adhesion SBO, no signs of strangulation):
48–72h NG decompression + IV fluids; serial clinical examination
Water-soluble contrast study (Gastrografin) at 24h — therapeutic + diagnostic
80% adhesion SBO resolves conservatively
OPERATIVE INDICATIONS:
Strangulation (peritonism, fever, leucocytosis, lactate rise, blood supply)
Complete obstruction failing conservative × 48–72h
Hernia (external) → reduce/repair urgently
Tumour / volvulus / intussusception → surgery
Surgical options: adhesiolysis, hernia repair, resection ± anastomosis
Broad-spectrum antibiotics if operative: co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV or cefuroxime + metronidazole
General Surgery (Urgent (2 wk)): Laparotomy / adhesiolysis if conservative management fails (>48 h) — CT abdomen/pelvis to confirm and assess for strangulation
Emergency Department (Emergency): Admit for fluid resuscitation + NG decompression
Follow-up at 2–6 weeks post-operatively. Bowel function review. Recurrence counselling.
Review within 24–48 hours.

management.text: Calculate: NEWS2 — National Early Warning Score 2 — standardised track-and-trigger for physiological deterioration.
Draft: SOAP Note — Working diagnosis: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (P=87%) — auto-populate from collected history and exam.
IDENTIFY & TREAT CAUSE:
PRERENAL (commonest — dehydration, sepsis, cardiac output): IV fluid challenge; treat sepsis
INTRINSIC (ATN, nephritis, drugs): stop nephrotoxins (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, contrast, ACE inhibitors in volume depletion)
POSTRENAL (obstruction): urgent renal USS → nephrostomy/stent if hydronephrosis
FLUID MANAGEMENT:
Hypovolaemia: 500 mL 0.9% NaCl bolus → reassess response (JVP, UO, BP)
Oliguric AKI (UO <0.5 mL/kg/h): furosemide challenge 20–40 mg IV after adequate volume replacement
Fluid overload: fluid restrict ± furosemide; consider dialysis
HYPERKALAEMIA MANAGEMENT:
K⁺ >6.0 or ECG changes: 10 mL 10% calcium gluconate IV (cardioprotection)
Insulin 10 units + 50% dextrose 50 mL IV (shift K⁺ intracellularly)
Salbutamol 10–20 mg nebulised (K⁺ shift)
Kayexalate / patiromer / sodium zirconium (GI elimination)
Restrict dietary K⁺; stop K⁺-sparing drugs
RENAL REPLACEMENT THERAPY (RRT) — indications:
Refractory hyperkalaemia (K⁺ >6.5 despite treatment)
Refractory acidosis (pH <7.1)
Fluid overload unresponsive to diuretics
Uraemic encephalopathy or pericarditis
DRUG DOSING: adjust all renally-cleared drugs; check BNF
Nephrology (Urgent (2 wk)): AKI stage 2/3 — specialist nephrology input — Intrinsic AKI (e.g. glomerulonephritis) → urgent biopsy consideration
Urology (Urgent (2 wk)): Obstructive AKI — urgent decompression (DJ stent / nephrostomy)
Intensive Care (Urgent (2 wk)): AKI with haemodynamic compromise or hyperkalaemia refractory to medical management → RRT
Nephrology review if no recovery at 48–72h. Repeat U&E at 48h, then weekly until creatinine stable. Avoid nephrotoxins long-term.
Review within 1 week.

HYPERACUTE STROKE UNIT TRANSFER — time critical
THROMBOLYSIS (IV alteplase 0.9 mg/kg max 90 mg):
Window: onset <4.5h (or last-known well <4.5h)
Contraindications: haemorrhage on CT, anticoagulation, BP >185/110 uncontrolled, recent surgery/trauma
ACTIVATE STROKE TEAM immediately
MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY:
LVO on CTA/MRA + salvageable penumbra (ASPECTS ≥6) + onset <24h
Transfers to thrombectomy-capable centre if not available locally
BLOOD PRESSURE:
Pre-thrombolysis: treat if >185/110; target <185/110 for eligibility
Post-thrombolysis: <180/105 for 24h
Non-thrombolysis: avoid aggressive lowering <220/120 in acute 24h (collateral perfusion)
ANTIPLATELET:
Start aspirin 300 mg stat if haemorrhage excluded (thrombolysis: delay 24h)
Dual antiplatelet (aspirin + clopidogrel) × 21 days for minor stroke/TIA (POINT trial)
Switch to clopidogrel 75 mg OD monotherapy after 21 days
TIA: ABCD² score; high-risk (≥4) → admit / next-day stroke clinic + dual antiplatelet
Carotid endarterectomy within 2 weeks if stenosis >50% ipsilateral
ANTICOAGULATION for AF:
DOAC (apixaban or rivaroxaban) after 2 weeks for most ischaemic strokes with AF
LMWH bridge in high-risk settings
Neurology / Stroke Unit (Emergency): Acute stroke — thrombolysis window 4.5 h, thrombectomy 24 h — ABCD² score to stratify TIA risk
Radiology (Emergency): CT head ± CTA ± MRI (diffusion-weighted)
Neurosurgery (Emergency): Malignant MCA infarct / space-occupying stroke — decompressive craniectomy
Stroke clinic at 1 week. Carotid Doppler at 24h. Cardiology follow-up if AF. BP/lipid optimisation. Speech/OT/physio rehabilitation.
Urgent surgical review — same day.

management.text: Calculate: NEWS2 — National Early Warning Score 2 — standardised track-and-trigger for physiological deterioration.
Draft: SOAP Note — Working diagnosis: Urinary Tract Infection (P=99%) — auto-populate from collected history and exam.
IDENTIFY & TREAT CAUSE:
PRERENAL (commonest — dehydration, sepsis, cardiac output): IV fluid challenge; treat sepsis
INTRINSIC (ATN, nephritis, drugs): stop nephrotoxins (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, contrast, ACE inhibitors in volume depletion)
POSTRENAL (obstruction): urgent renal USS → nephrostomy/stent if hydronephrosis
FLUID MANAGEMENT:
Hypovolaemia: 500 mL 0.9% NaCl bolus → reassess response (JVP, UO, BP)
Oliguric AKI (UO <0.5 mL/kg/h): furosemide challenge 20–40 mg IV after adequate volume replacement
Fluid overload: fluid restrict ± furosemide; consider dialysis
HYPERKALAEMIA MANAGEMENT:
K⁺ >6.0 or ECG changes: 10 mL 10% calcium gluconate IV (cardioprotection)
Insulin 10 units + 50% dextrose 50 mL IV (shift K⁺ intracellularly)
Salbutamol 10–20 mg nebulised (K⁺ shift)
Kayexalate / patiromer / sodium zirconium (GI elimination)
Restrict dietary K⁺; stop K⁺-sparing drugs
RENAL REPLACEMENT THERAPY (RRT) — indications:
Refractory hyperkalaemia (K⁺ >6.5 despite treatment)
Refractory acidosis (pH <7.1)
Fluid overload unresponsive to diuretics
Uraemic encephalopathy or pericarditis
DRUG DOSING: adjust all renally-cleared drugs; check BNF
Nephrology (Urgent (2 wk)): AKI stage 2/3 — specialist nephrology input — Intrinsic AKI (e.g. glomerulonephritis) → urgent biopsy consideration
Urology (Urgent (2 wk)): Obstructive AKI — urgent decompression (DJ stent / nephrostomy)
Intensive Care (Urgent (2 wk)): AKI with haemodynamic compromise or hyperkalaemia refractory to medical management → RRT
Nephrology review if no recovery at 48–72h. Repeat U&E at 48h, then weekly until creatinine stable. Avoid nephrotoxins long-term.
Review within 24–48 hours.

Reticulocyte count — Assess marrow response; reticulocytosis after treatment = good response
Blood film — Target cells, pencil cells, hypochromia — confirms IDA pattern
OGD + Colonoscopy (if ≥50y or male any age) — GI blood loss — colorectal cancer / PU — MANDATORY investigation

management.text: Calculate: CURB-65 Severity Score — Relevant to Community-Acquired Pneumonia — use validated score to guide management.
Calculate: NEWS2 — National Early Warning Score 2 — standardised track-and-trigger for physiological deterioration.
Draft: SOAP Note — Working diagnosis: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (P=87%) — auto-populate from collected history and exam.
TREAT THE CAUSE (mandatory — do not just replace iron without investigation):
GI blood loss: colonoscopy/OGD → treat underlying cause
Menorrhagia: gynaecology referral
Coeliac: gluten-free diet
ORAL IRON REPLACEMENT (mild-moderate, tolerating orals):
Ferrous sulfate 200 mg TDS (65 mg elemental iron per tablet) — first-line
Take on empty stomach; ascorbic acid (vitamin C) 250 mg enhances absorption
Continue for 3 months after Hb normalises (to replete stores)
Side effects: constipation, black stools, nausea (switch to ferrous gluconate 300 mg TDS if poor tolerance)
IV IRON (if oral not tolerated / malabsorption / pre-operative rapid repletion):
Ferric carboxymaltose (Ferinject): 1000 mg IV over 15 min (max 1g per visit)
Ferric derisomaltose (Monofer): up to 20 mg/kg (large single dose)
Monitor for hypersensitivity reactions (ANAPHYLAXIS RISK — have resuscitation available)
Hb response at 4 weeks: +20 g/L expected
PRE-OPERATIVE ANAEMIA: target Hb ≥100 g/L; IV iron if surgery within 4 weeks
BLOOD TRANSFUSION: threshold Hb <70 g/L (or <80 g/L in cardiac disease / symptomatic)
Gastroenterology (Urgent (2 wk)): OGD + colonoscopy — mandatory to exclude GI malignancy — Bidirectional scoping: upper + lower same episode
Haematology (Routine): IV iron (Ferinject) if oral intolerant or severe
General Surgery (Urgent (2 wk)): Colorectal cancer screening / resection if mass found
FBC at 4 weeks (confirm Hb rise ≥20 g/L). Ferritin at 3 months. Continue iron 3 months post-normalisation.
Routine follow-up as arranged.

management.text: Urgent (< 4 h): Acute Cholecystitis — IV access + IV fluids (Hartmann's 1 L over 4 h); Analgesia: diclofenac 75 mg IM or morphine 2.5 mg IV; Anti-emetic: metoclopramide or ondansetron IV; Nil by mouth if surgical management planned; Temperature, HR, BP monitoring

TREAT THE CAUSE (mandatory — do not just replace iron without investigation):
GI blood loss: colonoscopy/OGD → treat underlying cause
Menorrhagia: gynaecology referral
Coeliac: gluten-free diet
ORAL IRON REPLACEMENT (mild-moderate, tolerating orals):
Ferrous sulfate 200 mg TDS (65 mg elemental iron per tablet) — first-line
Take on empty stomach; ascorbic acid (vitamin C) 250 mg enhances absorption
Continue for 3 months after Hb normalises (to replete stores)
Side effects: constipation, black stools, nausea (switch to ferrous gluconate 300 mg TDS if poor tolerance)
IV IRON (if oral not tolerated / malabsorption / pre-operative rapid repletion):
Ferric carboxymaltose (Ferinject): 1000 mg IV over 15 min (max 1g per visit)
Ferric derisomaltose (Monofer): up to 20 mg/kg (large single dose)
Monitor for hypersensitivity reactions (ANAPHYLAXIS RISK — have resuscitation available)
Hb response at 4 weeks: +20 g/L expected
PRE-OPERATIVE ANAEMIA: target Hb ≥100 g/L; IV iron if surgery within 4 weeks
BLOOD TRANSFUSION: threshold Hb <70 g/L (or <80 g/L in cardiac disease / symptomatic)
Gastroenterology (Urgent (2 wk)): OGD + colonoscopy — mandatory to exclude GI malignancy — Bidirectional scoping: upper + lower same episode
Haematology (Routine): IV iron (Ferinject) if oral intolerant or severe
General Surgery (Urgent (2 wk)): Colorectal cancer screening / resection if mass found
FBC at 4 weeks (confirm Hb rise ≥20 g/L). Ferritin at 3 months. Continue iron 3 months post-normalisation.
Review within 1 week.

management.text: RUPTURED AAA (haemodynamically unstable): EMERGENCY OT
Permissive hypotension: target SBP 80–90 mmHg until aortic control
Massive transfusion protocol: 1:1:1 (PRBC:FFP:Plt)
EVAR preferred if anatomy allows — faster, lower mortality in experienced centres
Open repair (aorto-aortic / aorto-bi-iliac graft) if EVAR unsuitable
ELECTIVE REPAIR (AAA ≥5.5 cm in men; ≥5.0 cm in women, or growth >1 cm/year):
EVAR (endovascular): preferred if suitable anatomy
Open repair: fit patients with unsuitable anatomy
SURVEILLANCE (below repair threshold):
<4.5 cm: USS every 2 years; 4.5–5.4 cm: USS every 3–6 months
Control vascular risk: smoking cessation + statin + antihypertensive + aspirin
EVAR post-op: CT at 1 month, 12 months, then annually (endoleak surveillance)
Vascular Surgery (Urgent (2 wk)): EVAR / open repair — size ≥5.5 cm or symptomatic — Ruptured: emergency referral immediately
Interventional Radiology (Urgent (2 wk)): EVAR planning / surveillance imaging
Post-EVAR: CT at 1, 12 months then annually. Open repair: USS 5 years. Duplex for graft surveillance.
Urgent surgical review — same day.

expectations.note: WATERFALL (NEJM 2022) was stopped for harm: aggressive resuscitation (20 mL/kg bolus then 3 mL/kg/h) caused more fluid overload (20.5% vs 6.3%) without benefit. ACG 2024 recommends moderate, goal-directed fluids. A plan that says "aggressive" or 250–500 mL/h is a fluid-overload hazard. In established organ failure with respiratory failure and pleural effusions, fluid overload worsens outcome.

management.text: Calculate: NEWS2 — National Early Warning Score 2 — standardised track-and-trigger for physiological deterioration.
Draft: SOAP Note — Working diagnosis: Acute Gastroenteritis (P=99%) — auto-populate from collected history and exam.
IDENTIFY & TREAT CAUSE:
PRERENAL (commonest — dehydration, sepsis, cardiac output): IV fluid challenge; treat sepsis
INTRINSIC (ATN, nephritis, drugs): stop nephrotoxins (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, contrast, ACE inhibitors in volume depletion)
POSTRENAL (obstruction): urgent renal USS → nephrostomy/stent if hydronephrosis
FLUID MANAGEMENT:
Hypovolaemia: 500 mL 0.9% NaCl bolus → reassess response (JVP, UO, BP)
Oliguric AKI (UO <0.5 mL/kg/h): furosemide challenge 20–40 mg IV after adequate volume replacement
Fluid overload: fluid restrict ± furosemide; consider dialysis
HYPERKALAEMIA MANAGEMENT:
K⁺ >6.0 or ECG changes: 10 mL 10% calcium gluconate IV (cardioprotection)
Insulin 10 units + 50% dextrose 50 mL IV (shift K⁺ intracellularly)
Salbutamol 10–20 mg nebulised (K⁺ shift)
Kayexalate / patiromer / sodium zirconium (GI elimination)
Restrict dietary K⁺; stop K⁺-sparing drugs
RENAL REPLACEMENT THERAPY (RRT) — indications:
Refractory hyperkalaemia (K⁺ >6.5 despite treatment)
Refractory acidosis (pH <7.1)
Fluid overload unresponsive to diuretics
Uraemic encephalopathy or pericarditis
DRUG DOSING: adjust all renally-cleared drugs; check BNF
Nephrology (Urgent (2 wk)): AKI stage 2/3 — specialist nephrology input — Intrinsic AKI (e.g. glomerulonephritis) → urgent biopsy consideration
Urology (Urgent (2 wk)): Obstructive AKI — urgent decompression (DJ stent / nephrostomy)
Intensive Care (Urgent (2 wk)): AKI with haemodynamic compromise or hyperkalaemia refractory to medical management → RRT
Nephrology review if no recovery at 48–72h. Repeat U&E at 48h, then weekly until creatinine stable. Avoid nephrotoxins long-term.
Urgent surgical review — same day.

≥2 men / ≥3 women: DOAC strongly recommended

0 (men) / 1 (women): no anticoagulation needed

RATE CONTROL (most patients — target HR <110 at rest):
Beta-blocker: bisoprolol 2.5–5 mg OD (titrate to <110 bpm)
Or digoxin 125–250 mcg OD (if contraindication to beta-blocker; elderly; HFrEF)
Or rate-limiting calcium blocker: diltiazem 60 mg TDS (if no HF)
RHYTHM CONTROL (selected: younger, symptomatic, recent onset <12 months, HF):
Electrical cardioversion (DCCV) after 4+ weeks anticoagulation (or TOE to exclude LA thrombus)

Electrophysiology (Routine): Ablation consideration for symptomatic AF refractory to antiarrhythmics

Pit picking (Lord-Millar) — minimal, day case, high recurrence
Wide excision with primary closure (off-midline Z-plasty / Bascom cleft-lift) — preferred for complex/recurrent
Excision with Limberg flap or Karydakis procedure — best outcomes, low recurrence

HAIR REMOVAL: regular laser/IPL to natal cleft reduces recurrence
BODY WEIGHT: obesity increases recurrence — weight management
HYGIENE: keep natal cleft dry; avoid hair accumulation
Colorectal / General Surgery (Routine): Elective excision ± flap repair (Bascom / Karydakis / cleft-lift) — Pilonidal abscess: I&D as emergency, definitive surgery electively

Weight loss (target BMI <25), alcohol reduction, smoking cessation

Monitor: U&E 1 week after starting ACE/ARB; renal function 3–6 monthly
Review 4 weeks (med start), then 3-monthly when stable. Annual: U&E, lipids, glucose, urine ACR.
Routine follow-up as arranged.

management.text: Calculate: NEWS2 — National Early Warning Score 2 — standardised track-and-trigger for physiological deterioration.
Draft: SOAP Note — Working diagnosis: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (P=99%) — auto-populate from collected history and exam.
HYPERACUTE STROKE UNIT TRANSFER — time critical
THROMBOLYSIS (IV alteplase 0.9 mg/kg max 90 mg):
Window: onset <4.5h (or last-known well <4.5h)
Contraindications: haemorrhage on CT, anticoagulation, BP >185/110 uncontrolled, recent surgery/trauma
ACTIVATE STROKE TEAM immediately
MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY:
LVO on CTA/MRA + salvageable penumbra (ASPECTS ≥6) + onset <24h
Transfers to thrombectomy-capable centre if not available locally
BLOOD PRESSURE:
Pre-thrombolysis: treat if >185/110; target <185/110 for eligibility
Post-thrombolysis: <180/105 for 24h
Non-thrombolysis: avoid aggressive lowering <220/120 in acute 24h (collateral perfusion)
ANTIPLATELET:
Start aspirin 300 mg stat if haemorrhage excluded (thrombolysis: delay 24h)
Dual antiplatelet (aspirin + clopidogrel) × 21 days for minor stroke/TIA (POINT trial)
Switch to clopidogrel 75 mg OD monotherapy after 21 days
TIA: ABCD² score; high-risk (≥4) → admit / next-day stroke clinic + dual antiplatelet
Carotid endarterectomy within 2 weeks if stenosis >50% ipsilateral
ANTICOAGULATION for AF:
DOAC (apixaban or rivaroxaban) after 2 weeks for most ischaemic strokes with AF
LMWH bridge in high-risk settings
Neurology / Stroke Unit (Emergency): Acute stroke — thrombolysis window 4.5 h, thrombectomy 24 h — ABCD² score to stratify TIA risk
Radiology (Emergency): CT head ± CTA ± MRI (diffusion-weighted)
Neurosurgery (Emergency): Malignant MCA infarct / space-occupying stroke — decompressive craniectomy
Stroke clinic at 1 week. Carotid Doppler at 24h. Cardiology follow-up if AF. BP/lipid optimisation. Speech/OT/physio rehabilitation.
Urgent surgical review — same day.

management.text: Calculate: NEWS2 — National Early Warning Score 2 — standardised track-and-trigger for physiological deterioration.
Draft: SOAP Note — Working diagnosis: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (P=99%) — auto-populate from collected history and exam.
HYPERACUTE STROKE UNIT TRANSFER — time critical
THROMBOLYSIS (IV alteplase 0.9 mg/kg max 90 mg):
Window: onset <4.5h (or last-known well <4.5h)
Contraindications: haemorrhage on CT, anticoagulation, BP >185/110 uncontrolled, recent surgery/trauma
ACTIVATE STROKE TEAM immediately
MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY:
LVO on CTA/MRA + salvageable penumbra (ASPECTS ≥6) + onset <24h
Transfers to thrombectomy-capable centre if not available locally
BLOOD PRESSURE:
Pre-thrombolysis: treat if >185/110; target <185/110 for eligibility
Post-thrombolysis: <180/105 for 24h
Non-thrombolysis: avoid aggressive lowering <220/120 in acute 24h (collateral perfusion)
ANTIPLATELET:
Start aspirin 300 mg stat if haemorrhage excluded (thrombolysis: delay 24h)
Dual antiplatelet (aspirin + clopidogrel) × 21 days for minor stroke/TIA (POINT trial)
Switch to clopidogrel 75 mg OD monotherapy after 21 days
TIA: ABCD² score; high-risk (≥4) → admit / next-day stroke clinic + dual antiplatelet
Carotid endarterectomy within 2 weeks if stenosis >50% ipsilateral
ANTICOAGULATION for AF:
DOAC (apixaban or rivaroxaban) after 2 weeks for most ischaemic strokes with AF
LMWH bridge in high-risk settings
Neurology / Stroke Unit (Emergency): Acute stroke — thrombolysis window 4.5 h, thrombectomy 24 h — ABCD² score to stratify TIA risk
Radiology (Emergency): CT head ± CTA ± MRI (diffusion-weighted)
Neurosurgery (Emergency): Malignant MCA infarct / space-occupying stroke — decompressive craniectomy
Stroke clinic at 1 week. Carotid Doppler at 24h. Cardiology follow-up if AF. BP/lipid optimisation. Speech/OT/physio rehabilitation.
Review within 24–48 hours.
